podcast.title: Early Piano Lessons and Beatles Influence
podcast.body: Tim Rice-Oxley took piano lessons as a teenager but became disengaged by the classical curriculum. He subsequently ceased formal lessons and developed his unique style primarily through extensive listening to The Beatles' records, which became a significant influence on his musical approach. "One took piano lessons as a teenager, but grew tired of all the classical material he had to play. So he stopped with the lessons and started listening to a lot of Beatles records, and that's where most of his style developed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shift from Bass to Piano in Keane
podcast.body: Initially the bass player for Keane, Tim Rice-Oxley transitioned to piano after the band's guitarist departed around five years into their formation, leaving a "big hole" in their sound. This change allowed him to fulfill his desire to play piano, specifically favoring non-digital instruments. "He'd been the bass player until that point, and although he wanted to play the piano, he really didn't want to use anything digital."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signature Piano Sound with Yamaha CP70BM
podcast.body: Tim Rice-Oxley acquired a Yamaha CP70BM, a hybrid acoustic electric grand piano, after learning that Beatles producer George Martin highly regarded it. Upon tracking down a used one and plugging it in, the instrument produced a "massive sound" that immediately became Keane's defining characteristic and opened up new musical possibilities, leading to alt rock hits. "He acquired a Yamaha CP70BM, a hybrid acoustic electric grand piano, after reading that the Beatles producer George Martin really liked this thing. He eventually tracked down a used one, and here's a quote, as soon as we plugged it in, it made this massive sound, and we immediately knew it was the sound of Keene."

xref.title: Childhood Connection and Shared School
xref.body: Tom Chaplin eventually met Tim Rice-Oxley's brother, Tim. They later attended the same private school, which was owned by Tom Chaplin's family, fostering their early connection. "Now, eventually, Tom Chaplin met up with Tom Rice Oxley's brother Tim. They later ended up at the same private school, which was owned by Tom's family."

xref.title: Defining Sound with Yamaha CP70BM
xref.body: Following their guitarist's departure, Tim Rice-Oxley acquired a Yamaha CP70BM, a hybrid acoustic electric grand piano, influenced by Beatles producer George Martin's preference for the instrument. Plugging it in produced a "massive sound" that instantly became the signature sound of Keane, distinguishing them by centering their music around the piano rather than the guitar, leading to alt rock hits. "as soon as we plugged it in, it made this massive sound, and we immediately knew it was the sound of Keene. It opened up everything for the band, which started having all rock hits like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shared Birthday and Parental Friendship
xref.body: Singer Tom Chaplin and pianist Tim Rice-Oxley were both born on March 8, 1979. Their mothers bonded over having newborns with the same birthday and subsequently became friends. "This was the day that singer Tom Chaplin was born, and it was also the same birthday as a guy named Tom Rice Oxley, the two mothers bonded over newborns, and they became friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tim Rice-Oxley Declined Coldplay Offer
xref.body: Tim Rice-Oxley, a skilled piano player, was asked by Chris Martin to join his band, Coldplay, but Tim declined the offer. He believed that Keane had a better chance of success. "By this time, Tim Rice Oxley was a pretty good piano player, and some dude named Chris Martin was so impressed. He had asked him to join his band, which was called Coldplay. Tim thought that Keene was a better bat, so he said no to Chris."
